basic.title: Staff Data Scientist, ML Platform
basic.summary: ML and AI platform engineer with nine years across the model lifecycle, from insurance risk modeling to enterprise AI industrialization and Generative AI systems. Work spans data and feature pipelines, training, retrieval, evaluation, model serving and production monitoring, with a platform bias toward reproducible and governed systems that continue performing after launch. Currently focused on MLOps, enterprise RAG and agentic AI, including evaluation harnesses, knowledge pipelines, deployment workflows and the controls that keep unvalidated or ungrounded AI workloads off production surfaces.

experience.title: Staff Data Scientist
bullets: Led engineering across Rackspace's FAIR AI industrialization platform and RITA enterprise AI assistant, helping move AI use cases from experimentation into secure, production-ready systems used across enterprise workflows.

Built the application, data, and AI architecture behind grounded enterprise-assistant experiences, connecting internal knowledge and operational systems to retrieval, reasoning, evaluation, and governed action workflows.

Developed reusable platform capabilities for training, retrieval, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management so AI and machine-learning workloads could move through a consistent production path rather than team-specific implementations.

Led architecture and production-readiness work across backend, AI/ML, data, cloud, reliability, and governance concerns, including performance, observability, security controls, release quality, and engineering standards.
experience.notes: FAIR and RITA are used as the Rackspace project anchor. Numeric impact figures and candidate-specific implementation details are synthetic test data for resume-generation testing unless independently verified; preserve the non-round metric style but replace unsupported figures before live submission.

experience.title: Senior Machine Learning Data Scientist
bullets: Delivered end-to-end software, data, and machine-learning systems across enterprise consulting engagements, owning technical discovery through production deployment and client handoff.
Built backend services, APIs, data pipelines, and cloud integrations that connected legacy enterprise systems with modern analytics and ML capabilities while keeping client-facing contracts stable.

Applied predictive modeling, NLP, forecasting, retrieval, and decision-support techniques where the client problem justified them, with reproducible evaluation and explicit production-quality gates rather than demo-only models.

Established deployment, observability, data-quality, security, and post-release operating practices as part of the engagement deliverable so client teams could tell whether a system was still healthy after handoff.
experience.notes: Consulting role intentionally kept industry-neutral in the profile. At generation, projects/shared.json supplies the JD-matched anonymized client engagement(s); the Avanade hidden corpus supplies technology-specific implementation evidence. Candidate-specific implementation details and metrics are synthetic/inferred test material unless independently verified.

experience.title: AI/ML Engineer
bullets: Built machine-learning and backend components for network-operations workflows, turning telemetry, device events, and performance data into actionable signals for teams managing large production environments.
Built feature and data-processing pipelines that normalized telemetry from heterogeneous systems before training and inference, reducing inconsistent inputs that had been degrading model evaluation.
Developed Python services that exposed model-derived risk and anomaly signals to operational workflows, moving ML results out of notebooks and into systems engineers could use during investigations.
Introduced experiment tracking, model versioning, and containerized deployment with rollback support, giving the team a repeatable production path as the number of operational models increased.

experience.title: Data Scientist
bullets: Built statistical and machine-learning models supporting underwriting and pricing decisions, moving risk assessment from manually maintained rules toward data-driven scoring.
Developed gradient-boosted and generalized linear models over policy, claims, and customer history, improving risk-tier separation by 23% against the incumbent rules-based approach.
Built scheduled scoring and ETL workflows that consolidated policy, claims, and customer sources into a shared analytical dataset used by modeling and reporting workloads.
Created Power BI and SQL reporting that gave underwriting and actuarial teams one shared view of risk scores, portfolio trends, and model behavior instead of parallel spreadsheets.
experience.notes: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: the 23% risk-tier separation figure is illustrative; base resume bullets were unquantified. Dates corrected to match LinkedIn (Data Scientist began Jan 2018, not Jul 2017).

note: Final Andrew universal-corpus design. Rackspace retains the 93-selector FAIR/RITA anchor corpus. Avanade is rebuilt as a dynamic consulting corpus with 101 selector families and 505 hidden bullets. For Avanade, no technology selector owns a client vertical: projects/shared.json selects the JD-relevant anonymized client engagement(s), and the hidden corpus contributes only reusable technical implementation depth, debugging/performance texture, reliability/security controls, and production handoff patterns. This combines Deepankar-style dynamic consulting-industry selection with Rhazel/Deep-style dense stack coverage while avoiding hard-coded industry conflicts. Candidate-specific implementations and quantitative impacts are synthetic/inferred resume-generation material unless independently verified before live use.
